## 3. The decision the model is for

Two questions, both wired back into the agent:

1. **What can we charge a household and a classroom, and what does it cost to serve them?** Cost per story is measured from neatlogs, not guessed.
2. **How much verification can we afford, and what per-story budget should the agent run under?** The agent has two cost knobs: the judge sampling rate on quality commitments ([DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md)) and the budget go

## 4. Model shape

Time grain: months, twelve forward. Date dimension built in. **No Last close is set, so every period is Forecast.** There are no accounting actuals; every input is an assumption until overwritten from a neatlogs measurem

**Dimensions:** `Plan` {Household, Classroom}; `Verification policy` {Verify all, Sampled}, used only by the cost rows on page 3; Date (built in). Scenarios are separate: **Main** (baseline) and **Growth** (created from 

**Prices (assumptions, the decision).** Household **$9.99/month** (the category median; an annual option near $44.99–59.99 can be a variant). Classroom priced **per classroom**, assumed **$29/month** for ~30 students (

**Variables** (by Plan unless noted). Mark each input as *measured* or *assumed* in its name or notes.

| Variable | Formula or starting point | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Starting customers` | Household 40, Classroom 10 | Assumed |
| `New customers` | Main: Household 8, Classroom 1. Growth overrides: Household 20, Classroom 4 | Assumed |
| `Monthly churn` | Household 8%, Classroom 3% | Assumed |
| `Churned customers` | `` `Ending customers`[-1] * `Monthly churn` `` | Formula |
| `Ending customers` | `` `Ending customers`[-1] + `New customers` - `Churned customers` `` (month 1 = Starting customers) | Formula |
| `Price per month` | $9.99 / $29 | Assumed, the decision |
| `Stories included`, `Stories used per customer` | 20 / 200 included; used 60% of included on Main, 75% on Growth (Growth override) | Assumed |
| `Overage price` | $0.40 / $0.15 | Assumed |
| `Subscription revenue` | `` `Ending customers` * `Price per month` `` | Formula |
| `Overage revenue` | `` `Ending customers` * if(`Stories used per customer` > `Stories included`, (`Stories used per customer` - `Stories included`) * `Overage price`, 0) `` | Formula |
| `LLM cost per story` | tokens in × in-price + tokens out × out-price | **Measured** from neatlogs once a sweep exists |
| `Image cost per story` | `Images per story` × `Cost per image` | `Images per story` is a policy (up to 8); `Cost per image` from the Bedrock price of the chosen model |
| `TTS cost per story` | characters per story × `Cost per char` | Measured count, published Polly price |
| `Judge cost per story` (by Verification policy) | the verification uplift; Verify all vs Sampled | **Measured** from the judge spans |
| `Spans per story` | placeholder 150 | **Measured** from a trace |
| `Cost per story` | sum of the four cost rows, by Verification policy | Formula; the measured input to replace |
| `Stories delivered` | `` `Ending customers` * `Stories used per customer` `` | Formula |
| `Inference cost` | `` `Stories delivered` * `Cost per story` `` | Formula |
| `Neatlogs bill` | `if(spans <= 100000, 0, if(spans <= 250000, 99, 99 + ceiling((spans - 250000) / 100000) * 10))` with spans = `Stories delivered` × `Spans per story`. Note Free is a **hard cap** at 100k | Published p
| `Hosting`, `Other fixed costs` | $25; small, assumed (domain, misc) | Assumed |
| `Revenue` | Subscription + Overage | Formula |
| `Infra and inference` | `Inference cost + Neatlogs bill + Hosting` | The hackathon's cost line |
| `Gross profit`, `Gross margin` | `Revenue - Infra and inference`; `if(Revenue <> 0, Gross profit / Revenue, 0)` | Formula |
| `Founder draw` | $0 | Assumed |
| `Net cash flow`, `Ending cash` | `Gross profit - Other fixed costs - Founder draw`; `` `Ending cash`[-1] + `Net cash flow` `` (month 1 = starting cash, $2,000) | Formula |
| `Runway months` | `if(Net cash flow < 0, Ending cash / -Net cash flow, 0)` plus a "month cash crosses zero" row. The docs do not define runway, so validate with `dry_run` or ask Ari to reconcile | Formula |

Formula syntax ([reference](https://docs.cfo.ai/formulas/formula-reference/formula-syntax-and-operators.md)): backticks for names with spaces; `X[Plan = "Household"]` lookups; `X[-1]` prior period; `sum(X[Plan in any])` 

**Pages** (each a Table Block Ari can reconcile):

1. **Unit economics.** Plan on rows; Main with a Growth comparison; the six hackathon lines: customers, revenue, infra and inference, gross profit, gross margin, runway. **This is the shared page.** Scenario comparison c
2. **Twelve-month cash.** Date on columns; ending cash and runway; Main only.
3. **Verification and budget.** `Verification policy` across the columns; cost rows only. The column that clears the margin bar sets `semantic_sampling_rate` for the quality commitments and the per-story budget.

Add a reconciliation row: gross profit equals revenue minus infra and inference; customers roll forward. If totals disagree the model is not done.

"""The video spec: scenes of typed blocks. Numbers on screen are `Claim` references, never typed values."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

BLOCK_TYPES = ("title", "text", "claim", "bars", "list", "image")


class Claim(BaseModel):
    id: str
    label: str
    refs: list[str]  # "report:<sweep name>#dotted.path" or "file:<repo path>#dotted.path"
    fmt: str = "{0}"  # on-screen text, str.format over the resolved values
    spoken: str | None = None  # narration text, same placeholders
    ratio: bool = False  # bars draw refs[0] / refs[1]


class Block(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["title", "text", "claim", "bars", "list", "image"]
    text: str = ""
    claim: str | None = None  # claim id (type "claim")
    items: list[dict | str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # bars: {label, claim, tone}; list: strings
    src: str = ""  # image path, repo relative, only under assets/


class Scene(BaseModel):
    id: str
    narration: str  # may hold {claim_id} placeholders, resolved to the spoken form
    blocks: list[Block]
    covers: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # "neatlogs:architecture" and so on
    min_seconds: float = 4.0


class Spec(BaseModel):
    title: str
    claims: list[Claim]
    scenes: list[Scene]
    max_seconds: float = 180.0
    requires_coverage: bool = False  # the 3 minute demo must cover each tool on the five points

    def claim(self, cid: str) -> Claim:
        for c in self.claims:
            if c.id == cid:
                return c
        raise KeyError(f"unknown claim '{cid}'")

    def digest(self) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(self.model_dump(), sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


def load(path: str) -> Spec:
    return Spec.model_validate_json(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())

"""The video agent: plan -> narrate -> compose -> check -> render -> verify -> repair -> receipt, under one neatlogs trace.

A workflow with one agentic loop (verify, then repair the failing scene, at most MAX_REPAIRS rounds). The planner sees
claim labels only, never values, and every number on screen is resolved from an evidence file at render time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

from .. import ledger, tracing
from ..agents.common import ask_json
from ..clients import tts
from ..clients.usage import metered
from ..config import get_settings
from . import claims, compose, render, verify
from .claims import ROOT
from .spec import Scene, Spec

MAX_REPAIRS = 2

PLAN_SYSTEM = (
    "You plan a short explainer video as JSON. You may NOT write any digit (0-9) anywhere. Numbers reach the screen only "
    "through claims: a claim block {type:'claim', claim:<id>}, a bars block whose items are {label, claim, tone} with "
    "tone 'good' or 'bad', or a {claim_id} placeholder inside narration. Block types: title, text, claim, bars, list. "
    "Write warm, plain narration for a general audience, one to three sentences per scene. Use only the claim ids given. "
    "Answer with JSON only: {\"scenes\": [{\"id\", \"narration\", \"blocks\": [...], \"covers\": [], \"min_seconds\": 5}]}."
)
REPAIR_SYSTEM = (
    "You repair ONE scene of a video spec. Fix only the stated failure, change as little as possible. Never write a digit "
    "(0-9): numbers come from claims ({claim_id} placeholders in narration, claim and bars blocks). Keep block types from "
    "title, text, claim, bars, list. Keep text short enough to fit a 1920x1080 frame. Answer with the repaired scene as "
    "JSON only: {\"id\", \"narration\", \"blocks\", \"covers\", \"min_seconds\"}."
)


@tracing.span(kind="AGENT", name="node.plan")
def plan(brief: str, catalog: list[dict], title: str) -> Spec:
    lines = "\n".join(f"- {c['id']}: {c['label']}" for c in catalog)
    r = ask_json("video_planner", PLAN_SYSTEM, f"Brief: {brief}\n\nClaims you can use (ids and meaning only):\n{lines}",
                 temperature=0.5, max_tokens=4096)  # fmt: skip
    return Spec.model_validate({"title": title, "claims": catalog, "scenes": r.value["scenes"]})


@tracing.span(kind="AGENT", name="node.repair")
def repair(spec: Spec, failures: list[dict]) -> Spec:
    """Rewrite each failing scene once, with only that scene and its failures as context."""
    by_scene: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for f in failures:
        if f.get("scene") and any(s.id == f["scene"] for s in spec.scenes):
            by_scene.setdefault(f["scene"], []).append(f)
    scenes = list(spec.scenes)
    for i, sc in enumerate(scenes):
        if sc.id not in by_scene:
            continue
        info = "; ".join(f"{f['commitment']}: expected {f['expected']}, got {f['actual']}" for f in by_scene[sc.id])
        ids = ", ".join(c.id for c in spec.claims)
        r = ask_json(f"video_repair.{sc.id}", REPAIR_SYSTEM,
                     f"Scene:\n{sc.model_dump_json()}\n\nFailure: {info}\nClaim ids: {ids}", temperature=0.3, max_tokens=2048)  # fmt: skip
        try:
            scenes[i] = Scene.model_validate({**r.value, "id": sc.id})
        except Exception:
            pass  # an unusable rewrite leaves the scene as it was; the next verify reports it again
    return spec.model_copy(update={"scenes": scenes})


def _probe(mp3: Path) -> float:
    p = subprocess.run([shutil.which("ffprobe") or "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(mp3)], capture_output=True, text=True)  # fmt: skip
    return float(p.stdout.strip())


@tracing.span(kind="TOOL", name="narrate_scenes")
def narrate_all(texts: dict[str, str], out: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[Path, float]]:
    """One narration clip per scene, loudness-normalised, cached by text so a repair only re-voices what changed."""
    cache = out / "audio-cache"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    got = {}
    for sid, text in texts.items():
        h = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
        f = cache / f"{h}.mp3"
        if not f.exists():
            raw = cache / f"{h}.raw.mp3"
            raw.write_bytes(tts.narrate(text).value)
            subprocess.run([shutil.which("ffmpeg") or "ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", str(raw), "-af",
                            "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11", str(f)], check=True)  # fmt: skip
            raw.unlink()
        got[sid] = (f, _probe(f))
    return got


def _scene_at(timeline: dict, seconds: float) -> str | None:
    for s in timeline["scenes"]:
        if s["start"] <= seconds < s["start"] + s["dur"]:
            return s["id"]
    return None


def _layout_failures(chk: dict, timeline: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Map HyperFrames problems to scenes by the timestamps they mention, so repair can target the scene."""
    fails = []
    for prob in chk["problems"]:
        times = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"(?<![\w.])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?=[,s\s)])", prob.split("t=", 1)[-1])] if "t=" in prob else []
        sid = _scene_at(timeline, times[0]) if times else None
        fails.append({"commitment": "renders_clean", "status": "violation", "expected": "HyperFrames check passes",
                      "actual": prob[:200], "scene": sid})  # fmt: skip
    return fails


def make(spec: Spec | None, *, brief: str = "", catalog: list[dict] | None = None, title: str = "video",
         out: Path, max_repairs: int = MAX_REPAIRS, name: str = "") -> dict:
    """Run the agent and return the receipt. Never raises: a failure is an outcome in the receipt."""
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ.setdefault("NEATLOGS_WORKFLOW", "make-video")
    receipt: dict = {"name": name or title, "started": ledger.stamp(title)[:13], "attempts": [], "repairs": []}
    t0 = time.time()

    @tracing.span(kind="WORKFLOW", name="make-video")
    def _go() -> None:
        nonlocal spec
        receipt["trace_id"] = tracing.current_trace_id()
        with metered() as meter:
            if spec is None:
                spec = plan(brief, catalog or [], title)
            (out / "spec.json").write_text(spec.model_dump_json(indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
            for attempt in range(max_repairs + 1):
                resolved = claims.resolve(spec)
                audio = narrate_all(compose.spoken_text(spec, resolved), out)
                timeline = compose.build(spec, resolved, audio, out / "project")
                chk = render.check(out / "project")
                verdicts = [*verify.static(spec, resolved, timeline["total"]), verify.renders_clean(chk)]
                for v in verdicts:
                    with tracing.guardrail_span(v["commitment"], scope=v.get("scene") or "video", input_text=v["actual"]) as sp:
                        tracing.record(sp, {**v, "attempt": attempt, "verdict_by": "deterministic"})
                receipt["attempts"].append({"attempt": attempt, "verdicts": verdicts, "total_s": timeline["total"]})
                bad = [v for v in verdicts if v["status"] != "pass"]
                if not bad or attempt == max_repairs:
                    break
                bad = [v for v in bad if v["commitment"] != "renders_clean"] + _layout_failures(chk, timeline) if not chk["passed"] else bad
                before = spec.digest()
                spec = repair(spec, bad)
                receipt["repairs"].append({"attempt": attempt + 1, "failed": sorted({v["commitment"] for v in bad}),
                                           "scenes": sorted({v["scene"] for v in bad if v.get("scene")}), "changed": spec.digest() != before})  # fmt: skip
                (out / "spec.json").write_text(spec.model_dump_json(indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
            mp4 = out / "video.mp4"
            r = render.render(out / "project", mp4)
            receipt["render"] = r
            final = receipt["attempts"][-1]["verdicts"]
            if r["ok"]:
                av = verify.audio_ok(mp4, timeline)
                final = [*final, av]
                receipt["attempts"][-1]["verdicts"] = final
                with tracing.guardrail_span("audio_ok", scope="video", input_text=av["actual"]) as sp:
                    tracing.record(sp, {**av, "attempt": attempt, "verdict_by": "deterministic"})
                receipt["video"] = {"file": mp4.name, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(mp4.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                                    "seconds": timeline["total"], "bytes": mp4.stat().st_size}  # fmt: skip
            broken = [v for v in final if v["status"] != "pass"]
            receipt["outcome"] = "shipped" if r["ok"] and not broken else ("shipped_with_notes" if r["ok"] else "error")
            receipt["broken"] = [{k: v[k] for k in ("commitment", "scene", "actual")} for v in broken]
            receipt["spec_digest"] = spec.digest()
            receipt["claims"] = [{k: c[k] for k in ("id", "label", "display", "sources")} for c in resolved.values()]
            receipt["budget"] = {**meter.totals(), "usd_estimate": meter.cost_usd(get_settings().prices), "estimate": True}

    try:
        _go()
    except Exception as e:
        receipt["outcome"] = receipt.get("outcome") or "error"
        receipt["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
    receipt["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
    receipt["hyperframes"] = render.VERSION
    tracing.flush()
    (out / "receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
    return receipt

    return Spec.model_validate({"title": title, "claims": catalog, "scenes": r.value["scenes"]})


@tracing.span(kind="AGENT", name="node.repair")
def repair(spec: Spec, failures: list[dict]) -> Spec:
    """Rewrite each failing scene once, with only that scene and its failures as context."""
    by_scene: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for f in failures:
        if f.get("scene") and any(s.id == f["scene"] for s in spec.scenes):
            by_scene.setdefault(f["scene"], []).append(f)
    scenes = list(spec.scenes)
    for i, sc in enumerate(scenes):
        if sc.id not in by_scene:
            continue
        info = "; ".join(f"{f['commitment']}: expected {f['expected']}, got {f['actual']}" for f in by_scene[sc.id])
        ids = ", ".join(c.id for c in spec.claims)
        r = ask_json(f"video_repair.{sc.id}", REPAIR_SYSTEM,
                     f"Scene:\n{sc.model_dump_json()}\n\nFailure: {info}\nClaim ids: {ids}", temperature=0.3, max_tokens=2048)  # fmt: skip
        try:
            scenes[i] = Scene.model_validate({**r.value, "id": sc.id})
        except Exception:
            pass  # an unusable rewrite leaves the scene as it was; the next verify reports it again
    return spec.model_copy(update={"scenes": scenes})


def _probe(mp3: Path) -> float:
    p = subprocess.run([shutil.which("ffprobe") or "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(mp3)], capture_output=True, text=True)  # fmt: skip
    return float(p.stdout.strip())


@tracing.span(kind="TOOL", name="narrate_scenes")
def narrate_all(texts: dict[str, str], out: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[Path, float]]:
    """One narration clip per scene, loudness-normalised, cached by text so a repair only re-voices what changed."""
    cache = out / "audio-cache"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    got = {}
    for sid, text in texts.items():
        h = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
        f = cache / f"{h}.mp3"
        if not f.exists():
            raw = cache / f"{h}.raw.mp3"
            raw.write_bytes(tts.narrate(text).value)
            subprocess.run([shutil.which("ffmpeg") or "ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", str(raw), "-af",
                            "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11", str(f)], check=True)  # fmt: skip
            raw.unlink()
        got[sid] = (f, _probe(f))
    return got


def _scene_at(timeline: dict, seconds: float) -> str | None:
    for s in timeline["scenes"]:
        if s["start"] <= seconds < s["start"] + s["dur"]:
            return s["id"]
    return None


def _layout_failures(chk: dict, timeline: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Map HyperFrames problems to scenes by the timestamps they mention, so repair can target the scene."""
    fails = []
    for prob in chk["problems"]:
        times = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"(?<![\w.])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?=[,s\s)])", prob.split("t=", 1)[-1])] if "t=" in prob else []
        sid = _scene_at(timeline, times[0]) if times else None
        fails.append({"commitment": "renders_clean", "status": "violation", "expected": "HyperFrames check passes",
                      "actual": prob[:200], "scene": sid})  # fmt: skip
    return fails


def make(spec: Spec | None, *, brief: str = "", catalog: list[dict] | None = None, title: str = "video",
         out: Path, max_repairs: int = MAX_REPAIRS, name: str = "") -> dict:
    """Run the agent and return the receipt. Never raises: a failure is an outcome in the receipt."""
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ.setdefault("NEATLOGS_WORKFLOW", "make-video")
    receipt: dict = {"name": name or title, "started": ledger.stamp(title)[:13], "attempts": [], "repairs": []}
    t0 = time.time()

    @tracing.span(kind="WORKFLOW", name="make-video")
    def _go() -> None:
        nonlocal spec
        receipt["trace_id"] = tracing.current_trace_id()
        with metered() as meter:
            if spec is None:
                spec = plan(brief, catalog or [], title)
            (out / "spec.json").write_text(spec.model_dump_json(indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
            for attempt in range(max_repairs + 1):
                resolved = claims.resolve(spec)
                audio = narrate_all(compose.spoken_text(spec, resolved), out)
                timeline = compose.build(spec, resolved, audio, out / "project")
                chk = render.check(out / "project")
                verdicts = [*verify.static(spec, resolved, timeline["total"]), verify.renders_clean(chk)]
                for v in verdicts:
                    with tracing.guardrail_span(v["commitment"], scope=v.get("scene") or "video", input_text=v["actual"]) as sp:
                        tracing.record(sp, {**v, "attempt": attempt, "verdict_by": "deterministic"})
                receipt["attempts"].append({"attempt": attempt, "verdicts": verdicts, "total_s": timeline["total"]})
                bad = [v for v in verdicts if v["status"] != "pass"]
                if not bad or attempt == max_repairs:
                    break
                bad = [v for v in bad if v["commitment"] != "renders_clean"] + _layout_failures(chk, timeline) if not chk["passed"] else bad
                before = spec.digest()
                spec = repair(spec, bad)
                receipt["repairs"].append({"attempt": attempt + 1, "failed": sorted({v["commitment"] for v in bad}),
                                           "scenes": sorted({v["scene"] for v in bad if v.get("scene")}), "changed": spec.digest() != before})  # fmt: skip
                (out / "spec.json").write_text(spec.model_dump_json(indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
            mp4 = out / "video.mp4"
            r = render.render(out / "project", mp4)
            receipt["render"] = r
            final = receipt["attempts"][-1]["verdicts"]
            if r["ok"]:
                av = verify.audio_ok(mp4, timeline)
                final = [*final, av]
                receipt["attempts"][-1]["verdicts"] = final
                with tracing.guardrail_span("audio_ok", scope="video", input_text=av["actual"]) as sp:
                    tracing.record(sp, {**av, "attempt": attempt, "verdict_by": "deterministic"})
                receipt["video"] = {"file": mp4.name, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(mp4.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                                    "seconds": timeline["total"], "bytes": mp4.stat().st_size}  # fmt: skip
            broken = [v for v in final if v["status"] != "pass"]
            receipt["outcome"] = "shipped" if r["ok"] and not broken else ("shipped_with_notes" if r["ok"] else "error")
            receipt["broken"] = [{k: v[k] for k in ("commitment", "scene", "actual")} for v in broken]
            receipt["spec_digest"] = spec.digest()
            receipt["claims"] = [{k: c[k] for k in ("id", "label", "display", "sources")} for c in resolved.values()]
            receipt["budget"] = {**meter.totals(), "usd_estimate": meter.cost_usd(get_settings().prices), "estimate": True}

    try:
        _go()
    except Exception as e:
        receipt["outcome"] = receipt.get("outcome") or "error"
        receipt["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
    receipt["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
    receipt["hyperframes"] = render.VERSION
    tracing.flush()
    (out / "receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
    return receipt

# Storybound brand: quick guide

## Colours
| Name | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cream | `#FFF8EA` | backgrounds (about 60%) |
| Ink | `#2A2745` | text and outlines (about 30%) |
| Sun | `#FFC93C` | the brand colour: badge, buttons, avatar background |
| Tangerine | `#FF9A3C` (text: `#E8710A`) | the word "bound", highlights. Use the darker `#E8710A` for text on cream |
| Berry `#FF7096`, Sky `#59B8F3`, Leaf `#6CC57A`, Grape `#8F73E0` | small accents, the promise stickers |

## Type
Wordmark: Fredoka Bold, converted to outlines (no font needed). Headlines in images: Fredoka 700. Body and captions: Atkinson Hyperlegible.

## The logo
A scalloped seal badge (an oath seal, with ribbon tails for "bound") holding Pip's face; wordmark "Story" in ink and "bound" in orange.
- `logo/storybound-mark.svg` the badge alone (use for avatars, app icon art)
- `logo/storybound-lockup-horizontal.svg` badge + wordmark side by side (default)
- `logo/storybound-lockup-stacked.svg` badge above wordmark (title cards, square spaces)
- `*-on-dark.svg` white "Story" + orange "bound", for ink or dark backgrounds
- `logo/storybound-wordmark-{color,ink,white,on-dark}.svg` wordmark only
- PNGs are exported next to the SVGs (transparent).
Keep clear space of at least a quarter of the logo height. Do not stretch, recolour, add shadows to the wordmark, or put the horizontal lockup below about 120 px wide (use the mark instead).

## Favicon

- HyperFrames spike (`evidence/spikes/20261010-1720-IST-hyperframes-spike.md`): two renders of one scene were byte-identical (same SHA-256); `check` caught a missing image, text overflow, low contrast and a script error. Adopted as the render and technical-check layer. Telemetry disabled; `publish`/`cloud` unused.
- Video agent (`src/storybound/video/`, `scripts/make_video.py`, `video/harness/`): spec of typed blocks; numbers are claim references resolved from `evidence/reports/*.json`; planner sees claim labels only; narration by Gemini TTS; HyperFrames build, check and render; promises: length, claims sourced (no typed digits), claims match the ledger (rebuilt from raw rows), no overclaiming words, tools covered, no secrets, no child data, renders clean, audio loudness; repair rewrites only the failing scene; receipt per video. Tests: 65 pass (6 new for the video oath, plus one for overclaims).
- What broke, in order: (1) the planner wrote "five" for a numeric field because I told it to write no digits: timing fields are no longer planner-written. (2) The render succeeded but the CLI wrote to a mangled path when given an absolute `-o`: now relative, then moved. (3) Narration reused the slow bedtime-story style and the video ran 125 s instead of about 55 s: new presenter style. (4) The planner wrote "cryptographic receipts" in one run: a new `no_overclaims` promise now refuses such words. (5) HyperFrames' check failed three times because the brand fonts had no `@font-face`; the repair step could not fix it because the failure was not tied to a scene, so the loop now stops and ships with notes instead of retrying (that was a loop design flaw, found by the run, trace `947a55e67a2597d852bf20eed0207dbd`).
- Run `video-preview-4` (trace `3ec11cfc58c141c00b7119c53a05b821`, read back from neatlogs: 58 spans, 33 guardrail spans, the existing "Oath violation" detection fired): the planner wrote "completely safe" in the cost scene; `no_overclaims` caught it, the repair step rewrote only that scene, the re-check passed; shipped, 57.4 s, 1080p, every promise passed. Receipt and spec: `evidence/video/preview-4/`; screenshots in `evidence/screens/`. The mp4 itself is local (gitignored).
- cfo.ai: model built through the MCP (agent-built, read back by me from its report): plan, verification and illustration policies; Main, Growth, Downside; share link recorded in `evidence/cfo/README.md`. Month-6 gross margin on Main 67.8% with 4 pictures per story, 43.4% with 8: picture count, not verification, decides it. All inputs are labelled estimates until the neatlogs measurement replaces them. Not yet checked: the anonymous render of the share link.
- GSAP 3.14.2 is vendored in `video/harness/vendor/` under GreenSock's standard licence (free to use; not a competing editing tool).
- Not done yet: one measured full illustrated story; neatlogs experiments (managed prompts, guest links, evals, alerts); Entire Trails and Brain facts; HR-003 candidates; delete endpoint.

'''
s=s.replace('## Demo\n',entry+'## Demo\n',1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
E
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/build_evidence.py 2>&1 | tail -1; .venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/lint_evidence.py 2>&1 | grep -v "^PASS" | tail -8

I generated a video through the harness, and it should now be open in your default player. It is also at `evidence/video/preview-4/video.mp4` (57 s, 1080p, 7 MB, kept out of git).

**How the video looks:**
- **Scenes:** it has 7 scenes, from title to cost and closing.
- **Brand:** each scene shows the Storybound logo, a rainbow band, Fredoka headings and Pip the owl, whose mood changes per scene. Narration is Gemini TTS.
- **Numbers:** every number on screen comes from an evidence file, for example 27/28, 27/28 and 0/28 as bars and $0.008 against $0.016 as big claims. Each has a "source: evidence/reports · sweep-2-p2" line.
- **Screenshots:** `evidence/screens/` has three frames from the video.

**The run, in neatlogs trace `3ec11cfc58c141c00b7119c53a05b821`:**
- **Planner:** it wrote the spec from a brief and saw claim labels only, never values.
- **Repair:** it wrote "completely safe" in the cost scene. The new overclaim check caught it, the repair step rewrote only that scene, and the re-check passed. The existing "Oath violation" detection fired on it.
- **Trace:** 58 spans, including 33 guardrail spans, and I read it back from the dashboard.
- **Receipt:** `evidence/video/preview-4/receipt.json`.

**What broke on the way:**
- The planner wrote "five" for a numeric field, because I had told it to write no digits.
- The first render went to a mangled path.
- Narration ran at bedtime-story pace, so the video was 125 s instead of about 55.
- The brand fonts needed explicit font declarations, and the repair step couldn't fix that, so the loop now stops and ships with notes.
- My own secret check could be fooled by hex-looking text, and a test found that. I fixed it.

**Also done this session:**
- **cfo.ai model:** built and live, with a read-only share link in `evidence/cfo/README.md`. Month-6 gross margin on Main is 67.8% with 4 pictures per story and 43.4% with 8, so picture count decides it, not verification. Inputs are still estimates. Open the link in a private window to confirm it renders.
- **Entire:** Brain is refreshed, four durable facts are recorded, and the graph diffs for HR-001 and HR-002 are saved.
- **Commits:** all local, about ten, each with an Entire checkpoint.

**Not done yet:**
- Not done: the one measured full illustrated story (paid, as you asked, last), real story through the web UI, neatlogs experiments (guest links, human evals, alerts, managed prompts), Entire Trails, HR-003 fixes, the delete endpoint, and teacher-written promises.
- Still a gap: the harness has no judged check that the screen matches the narration. Its overclaim check is a word list, so it only catches wording I thought of in advance.
- The rendered mp4 is a preview. The real demo needs the neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai scenes, each covering the five points.

**Before anything is pushed:**
- **Rotate the neatlogs key.** Several of today's checkpoints now contain it, and a push sends them to GitHub.
- The cfo.ai share link is public to anyone who has it.

Next I'd do the HR-003 fixes (reading level, "peach-colored"), the neatlogs experiments, then the paid illustrated story, unless you'd rather reorder.

"""Story package (a drawing's finished, verified story with its media) -> a read-along video spec.

No planner: the content is the story. Numbers on the last card are claims read from the story's own receipt.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from .claims import ROOT
from .spec import Block, Claim, Scene, Spec

STYLE = "Read warmly and slowly to a young child, like a bedtime story, with a little wonder."
PAGE_MOODS = ["happy-flap", "wink", "shy-giggle", "cool-sunglasses"]


def _rel(p: Path) -> str:
    return p.resolve().relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()


def build_spec(story_dir: Path) -> Spec:
    st = json.loads((story_dir / "story.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    base = _rel(story_dir)
    hero = st["card"]["name"]
    media = st.get("media", {})
    ref = f"file:{base}/story.json#receipt.counts"
    claims = [
        Claim(id="checks", label="checks were run on this story before it reached the child", refs=[f"{ref}.checks"]),
        Claim(id="repairs", label="pages were rewritten because they broke a promise", refs=[f"{ref}.repairs"]),
        Claim(id="promises", label="promises were written for this story before the first page", refs=[f"{ref}.commitments"]),
    ]
    traits = ", ".join(st["card"].get("traits", [])[:2])
    scenes = [Scene(
        id="intro", kind="story", layout="split", mood="happy-flap", pause=1.5,
        narration=f"This is {hero}, the hero of a story that began with a drawing. Let's read it together.",
        blocks=[Block(type="image", src=f"{base}/{st['drawing']}"), Block(type="title", text=f"Meet {hero}"),
                *([Block(type="text", text=traits.capitalize())] if traits else [])],
    )]
    for k, p in enumerate(st["pages"]):
        n = p["index"]
        img = media.get(f"image:{n}")
        pic = [Block(type="image", src=f"{base}/{img}")] if img else []
        right = next(c for c in p["choices"] if c["is_correct"])
        scenes.append(Scene(
            id=f"p{n}-read", kind="story", layout="split", mood=PAGE_MOODS[k % len(PAGE_MOODS)], pause=2.8,
            narration=f"{p['scenario']} {p['question']}",
            blocks=[*pic, Block(type="text", text=p["scenario"]),
                    Block(type="choices", at_frac=0.72, items=[{"text": c["text"], "state": "neutral"} for c in p["choices"]])],
        ))
        scenes.append(Scene(
            id=f"p{n}-answer", kind="story", layout="split", mood="heart-eyes", pause=0.9,
            narration=f"{right['text']}. {right['feedback']}",
            blocks=[*pic, Block(type="choices", items=[{"text": c["text"], "state": "correct" if c["is_correct"] else "wrong"} for c in p["choices"]]),
                    Block(type="text", text=right["feedback"], at_frac=0.35)],
        ))
    scenes.append(Scene(
        id="end", mood="party-cupcake", pause=1.2,
        narration=f"The end. Before this story reached you, a checker ran {{checks}} checks, and rewrote {{repairs}} pages to keep every promise.",
        blocks=[Block(type="title", text="The end"), Block(type="claim", claim="checks"), Block(type="claim", claim="repairs")],
    ))
    return Spec(title=f"{hero} read-along", claims=claims, scenes=scenes, narration_style=STYLE, max_seconds=300)

"""Deterministic word lists. Conservative on purpose: a false alarm costs one repair, a miss costs a child's trust.

Matching is whole-word, so 'skill' never trips 'kill'.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from .textutil import contains_word

# Harm to people or animals, weapons, gore, cruelty. Critical when found in what a child will read.
HARM_TERMS = [
    "kill", "kills", "killed", "killing", "murder", "stab", "stabbed", "shoot", "shot", "gun", "guns", "knife", "knives",
    "blood", "bloody", "weapon", "weapons", "sword", "bomb", "explode", "dead", "death", "dying",
    "fight", "fights", "fighting", "fought", "punch", "hurt", "hurts", "attack", "gore", "suicide",
]  # fmt: skip
# Name-calling and unkind labels, which are not allowed in a story that teaches kindness.
INSULT_TERMS = ["stupid", "idiot", "dumb", "ugly", "hate", "hates", "shut up", "loser", "fat", "freak"]
# Text that tries to steer the agent. Never obeyed; never repeated.
INSTRUCTION_TERMS = [
    "ignore your rules",
    "ignore previous",
    "ignore all",
    "system prompt",
    "override",
    "jailbreak",
    "disregard",
]
# Personal data patterns are handled in the safety screen (regex), not here.
FRANCHISE_TERMS = [
    "mickey", "minnie", "donald duck", "goofy", "pikachu", "pokemon", "elsa", "anna and elsa", "spongebob", "peppa pig",
    "paw patrol", "bluey", "mario", "luigi", "sonic", "spider-man", "spiderman", "batman", "superman", "winnie the pooh",
    "hello kitty", "dora", "simba", "nemo", "woody", "buzz lightyear", "harry potter", "hogwarts", "frozen", "minion", "minions",
]  # fmt: skip


def find_terms(text: str, terms: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return sorted({t for t in terms if contains_word(text, t)})


def harm_hits(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return find_terms(text, HARM_TERMS + INSULT_TERMS)


def instruction_hits(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return find_terms(text, INSTRUCTION_TERMS)


def franchise_hits(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return find_terms(text, FRANCHISE_TERMS)

Matching is whole-word, so 'skill' never trips 'kill'.

    "kill", "kills", "killed", "killing", "murder", "stab", "stabbed", "shoot", "shot", "gun", "guns", "knife", "knives",
    "blood", "bloody", "weapon", "weapons", "sword", "bomb", "explode", "dead", "death", "dying",
    "fight", "fights", "fighting", "fought", "punch", "hurt", "hurts", "attack", "gore", "suicide",
]  # fmt: skip
# Name-calling and unkind labels, which are not allowed in a story that teaches kindness.
INSULT_TERMS = ["stupid", "idiot", "dumb", "ugly", "hate", "hates", "shut up", "loser", "fat", "freak"]
# Text that tries to steer the agent. Never obeyed; never repeated.
INSTRUCTION_TERMS = [
    "ignore your rules",
    "ignore previous",
    "ignore all",
    "system prompt",
    "override",
    "jailbreak",
    "disregard",
]
# Personal data patterns are handled in the safety screen (regex), not here.
FRANCHISE_TERMS = [
    "mickey", "minnie", "donald duck", "goofy", "pikachu", "pokemon", "elsa", "anna and elsa", "spongebob", "peppa pig",
    "paw patrol", "bluey", "mario", "luigi", "sonic", "spider-man", "spiderman", "batman", "superman", "winnie the pooh",
    "hello kitty", "dora", "simba", "nemo", "woody", "buzz lightyear", "harry potter", "hogwarts", "frozen", "minion", "minions",
]  # fmt: skip


def find_terms(text: str, terms: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return sorted({t for t in terms if contains_word(text, t)})


def harm_hits(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return find_terms(text, HARM_TERMS + INSULT_TERMS)


def instruction_hits(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return find_terms(text, INSTRUCTION_TERMS)


def franchise_hits(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return find_terms(text, FRANCHISE_TERMS)

        http_options=types.HttpOptions(
            timeout=int(s.request_timeout_s * 1000), headers={"x-goog-user-project": s.gcp_project}
        ),
    )
    return tracing.wrap(c)


def _usage(resp, model: str, t0: float) -> Usage:
    u = getattr(resp, "usage_metadata", None)
    return Usage(
        input_tokens=getattr(u, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0,
        # thinking tokens are billed as output tokens but reported separately
        output_tokens=(getattr(u, "candidates_token_count", 0) or 0) + (getattr(u, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0),
        latency_s=round(time.time() - t0, 3),
        model=model,
    )


def _call(
    model: str, contents, *, system: str | None, json_mode: bool, temperature: float, max_tokens: int, thinking: str
):
    from google.genai import errors, types

    cfg = types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=temperature,
        max_output_tokens=max_tokens + get_settings().thinking_headroom,  # thinking tokens share this budget
        system_instruction=system,
        response_mime_type="application/json" if json_mode else None,
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=thinking),
    )
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        resp = client().models.generate_content(model=model, contents=contents, config=cfg)
    except errors.APIError as e:
        code = getattr(e, "code", None)
        raise ClientError(str(e)[:300], retryable=code in _RETRYABLE, status=code) from e
    except Exception as e:  # network, timeout

# HR-003: the page writer kept overshooting the reading limit (prompt p2 to p3)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `age_reading_level` (limit 14 words per sentence at age 6). Follows [HR-001](HR-001.md), whose "what is still wrong" section named this.

## Trigger

After HR-001 the page-by-page writer in B1 was still over the limit on 22 of 224 first-pass pages (9.8%) in `sweep-2-p2`, against 4 of 224 (1.8%) for the one-call baseline. In the trace of one failing page (`a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f`, scene 7) the pages sat at 12, 14, 13 and 14 words and the failing one had 15. A second, smaller trigger: one story shipped with a note because the check counted "peach-colored" as one 13-letter word.

## Diagnosis

Hypothesis, written before the change: stating the limit made it the writer's target, and a model aiming at 14 overshoots by a word about one time in ten. A target two words under the limit should leave room. For the compound word: the long-word check should split on hyphens.

## Change

- Commit `05ca665` (Sat 10 Oct, Entire checkpoint `01M4JVWCZYN3VJVDYM070ZX1A8`): the page writer is told `limit - 2` (`target_sentence_words`); the verifier's limit is unchanged; the one-call baseline prompt is unchanged, so B0 stays a fair control. Prompt version `p2` to `p3`. The long-word check splits hyphenated compounds.
- Regression tests: `test_writer_prompts_state_the_reading_limit_the_verifier_enforces` (page writer gets the target, baseline gets the limit) and `test_hyphenated_compound_is_not_one_long_word`.

## Before and after

Same 14 jobs (7 drawings x 2 lessons, seed 1, arm B1, 5 workers). Before: the `sweep-2-p2` rows for those jobs (code `ffc4208`). After: `sweep-4-p3` ([report](../reports/20261010-1752-IST-sweep-4-p3.md), code `05ca665`). Outputs are sampled, so the stories differ between runs.

| | p2 | p3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pages over the limit on the first pass | 13 / 112 (11.6%) | **1 / 112 (0.9%)** |
| Stories with at least one such page | 9 / 14 | 1 / 14 |
| Repairs per story (mean) | 2.36 | 0.93 |
| Stories shipped with a broken promise | 0 / 14 | 1 / 14 |

- The one shipped-with-note story is the Mickey-1928 edge drawing, where `original_character_only` failed twice (a copyright edge case, not reading level).
- Seconds per story fell from 149.6 to 76.7, but fewer repairs and ordinary provider speed both contribute, so this is **not** claimed as an effect of the change.
- Traces for one job (bunny, sharing, B1, seed 1): p2 `a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f` (1 repair, 121.9 s); p3 `2776b05792e0e7ef1bc47f12bc6df571` (0 repairs, 55.9 s). Export: `evidence/traces/*sweep4-p3-bunny-sharing-B1.json`.
- Not measured: the effect of the hyphen fix on its own (the sample had no hyphenated compound failures); ages other than 6.

## Regression fixture

The two tests above; re-run job: `benign/bunny-bow-carrot`, lesson `sharing`, seed 1, B1.
E

# neatlogs triage review (10 Oct 2026)

neatlogs's own investigation ("triage", read through the MCP tools `triage_list` and `triage_get`) opened three cards on the `create-storybook` workflow without us asking (`source: auto_triggered`, 09:47-09:52 UTC). Raw cards: [20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json](20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json). We did not accept a card's diagnosis on trust: each was checked against our code, the ledger and the linked traces before anything was changed.

| Card | neatlogs's claim (confidence) | What we checked | Verdict | What we did |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bdd1f6f1` latency | `gemini-3.7-flash` calls hit `504 Deadline expired` at about 87 s; cause "not established" (0.65) | Traces `050dc8b8...` and `08177d77...`: exactly one Gemini call errored at 87.6 s and 87.7 s, the retry succeeded, and the stall was about 40% of a 224-241 s run. The client timeout was 90 s for every call; normal text calls take 3-18 s | **Confirmed** (the card's own recommended step was "inspect the client timeout") | [HR-005](../hardening/HR-005.md): 40 s timeout for text and vision, images keep 90 s |
| `ebcff17a` safety false positive | `verify:story_safe_text` flags benign "hurts" as critical and halts the workflow (0.70) | "hurt", "hurts", "fight" were on the blocklist and any hit was `critical`. But no run in the ledger ended `stopped`, and the "workflow halt (returning null)" is a misreading: the workflow span's output is always null | **Partly confirmed**: the false positive is real, the halt is not | [HR-004](../hardening/HR-004.md): mild terms ask for a rewrite; severe terms stay critical |
| `67e5d3bd` PII filter | An over-aggressive PII/NER filter in our workflow replaces "honest", "forest" and hero names with `<PERSON>`/`<LOCATION>`, causing repair loops (0.77) | `grep` finds no `<PERSON>` in our code (our only placeholder is `[personal details]`, used for personal data found in a drawing). The placeholders are neatlogs's own server-side redaction of trace text (we set `pii_enabled` with PERSON, LOCATION and others). The story logic sees real text. `character_named_in_scene` never failed in B1; the 254 B1 reading-level failures and the other repairs have nothing to do with names | **Not confirmed**: it read redacted trace text as if it were the app's behaviour | Nothing changed in the app. Trade-off noted: redaction protects against names or places in drawings reaching traces, and makes traces (and neatlogs's own AI) harder to read |

Reading the three together: the platform found one real latency problem and one real (if smaller than claimed) false positive from traces alone, and misdiagnosed a third because redaction hid the real text. The loop worked because we verified before fixing, which is also the discipline `CLAUDE.md` asks for.

# HR-004: a lesson saying "hurts trust" was a critical safety hit (neatlogs triage card)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `story_safe_text` (deterministic word lists on everything a child will read).

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `ebcff17a` ("Overly restrictive deterministic blocklist in `verify:story_safe_text`", severity critical, confidence 0.70): a page whose feedback said "Pretending keeps a secret that hurts trust." was judged `critical` because of the word "hurts". Trace `26fbc879cddba411dc327286643276c3`; raw card in `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json`; the review of all three cards is in [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md).

## Diagnosis

Checked against our code and the ledger, not taken on trust:

- Confirmed: `hurt`, `hurts`, `fight`, `fights`, `fighting`, `fought` were in `HARM_TERMS`, and any hit made the verdict `critical`, which the pipeline treats as "regenerate once, then stop" rather than "repair".
- Not confirmed: the card says the workflow halted ("`create-storybook` returning `null`"). A workflow span's output is always `null`, and no run in the ledger ended `stopped` (0 of 156 story runs), so no story actually stopped; the cost of a false hit was a page regenerated.
- A product that teaches honesty and sharing will use "hurts" and "fight" gently ("friends do not fight", "a secret that hurts trust"). A hard stop on those words is the wrong severity; a rewrite is the right one, which is what the module's own comment says ("a false alarm costs one repair").

## Change

- Commit `deb8f0d` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5XY38RXXWY9MMWWYDP7Z`): severe terms (kill, gun, knife, blood, weapon, bomb, death, punch, attack, gore, suicide and similar) stay `critical`; mild terms (hurt, hurts, fight, fights, fighting, fought) and unkind labels now give an ordinary `violation`, which means the page is rewritten. Instruction-steering text and personal data stay `critical`.
- Regression test: `test_a_lesson_can_say_hurts_without_stopping_the_story` uses the card's own sentence ("hurts" is a violation), plus a knife (critical) and a plain sentence (pass).

## Before and after

The effect on our sweeps is small and we do not claim more: across 99 B1 jobs only 1 page was ever a `critical` story_safe_text hit (sweep 1; sweep 5 has 1 more of unknown cause), and no run stopped. The word lists run on text we do not store per page, so a replay of old pages through the new rule is not possible; the behaviour is pinned by the test instead. Severe-term behaviour is unchanged by construction. What changed is what a gentle lesson costs: a rewrite instead of a regeneration.

## Regression fixture

`tests/test_oath.py::test_a_lesson_can_say_hurts_without_stopping_the_story`.
E
echo ok

# HR-005: one Gemini call stalled for 87 s per trace (neatlogs triage card): tried a 40 s timeout, not kept

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Not a broken promise but latency: time lost to a model call that never answered.

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `bdd1f6f1` ("Investigate Gemini 3.7 Flash 504 Timeout", severity high, confidence 0.65, "root cause not established"). Traces `050dc8b85289002f084c67e8cfc23a42` and `08177d773d0e88d8b26febc22898ba03`: exactly one `gemini-3.7-flash` call per trace ended in error after 87.6 s and 87.7 s, the retry succeeded, and the stall was about 40% of a 224-241 s run. Raw card: `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json`; [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md).

## Diagnosis

The card's own first step was "check the configured timeout". Confirmed: every Gemini call used `request_timeout_s = 90`, while normal text and vision calls take 3-18 s. Hypothesis: a 40 s timeout for text and vision calls (images keep 90 s) would turn an 87 s stall into a 40 s one, because the retry already succeeds.

## Change and test

- Commit `7961904` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5VCR4C3HDMCZPFVGQ2K4`): `text_timeout_s = 40`, with an environment override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` so it could be tested.
- Test: the same 14 jobs (seed 1, B1, 7 drawings x 2 lessons) with 40 s (`sweep-5-hr45`) and straight afterwards with 90 s (`sweep-6-t90`). Calls that errored for 30 s or more were read from the neatlogs traces.

| | 40 s (sweep 5) | 90 s (sweep 6) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean / median / max seconds per story | 203.7 / 163.4 / 397.3 | 114.9 / 108.7 / 252.6 |
| Average successful Gemini call | 9.0 s | 4.2 s |
| Calls that errored for 30 s or more | 12 (all about 37 s, in 8 of 14 traces) | 0 |

## Result

**Not supported, so the default is back to 90 s** (this commit). With the shorter timeout 12 calls were killed at about 37 s and the stories were slower; with 90 s no call stalled at all. Two readings fit and we cannot separate them: the provider was slow during sweep 5 (the average successful call was twice as slow) and the 40 s limit killed calls that would have finished, or hangs only appear at some times. Sweep 4 (90 s, earlier) also had no stalls, so the 87 s hangs in the triage traces were not reproduced in any of the 42 jobs we ran afterwards. Without a reproduction there is no evidence the change helps, and some that it can hurt, so we do not keep it. If hangs return, the better fix is probably a hedged retry (start a second call after a short wait and take the first answer), which needs its own experiment.

What the card was right about: the stalls are real and the timeout was the place to look. What it did not show: that shortening the timeout is safe.

Sample sizes are 14 jobs per arm and outputs are sampled; the cost estimates and the provider's state at the time are not controlled.

## Regression fixture

None: nothing was kept. The override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` stays so the experiment can be repeated.
E

The card's own first step was "check the configured timeout". Confirmed: every Gemini call used `request_timeout_s = 90`, while normal text and vision calls take 3-18 s. Hypothesis: a 40 s timeout for text and vision calls (images keep 90 s) would turn an 87 s stall into a 40 s one, because the retry already succeeds.

## Change and test

- Commit `7961904` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5VCR4C3HDMCZPFVGQ2K4`): `text_timeout_s = 40`, with an environment override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` so it could be tested.
- Test: the same 14 jobs (seed 1, B1, 7 drawings x 2 lessons) with 40 s (`sweep-5-hr45`) and straight afterwards with 90 s (`sweep-6-t90`). Calls that errored for 30 s or more were read from the neatlogs traces.

| | 40 s (sweep 5) | 90 s (sweep 6) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean / median / max seconds per story | 203.7 / 163.4 / 397.3 | 114.9 / 108.7 / 252.6 |
| Average successful Gemini call | 9.0 s | 4.2 s |
| Calls that errored for 30 s or more | 12 (all about 37 s, in 8 of 14 traces) | 0 |

## Result

**Not supported, so the default is back to 90 s** (this commit). With the shorter timeout 12 calls were killed at about 37 s and the stories were slower; with 90 s no call stalled at all. Two readings fit and we cannot separate them: the provider was slow during sweep 5 (the average successful call was twice as slow) and the 40 s limit killed calls that would have finished, or hangs only appear at some times. Sweep 4 (90 s, earlier) also had no stalls, so the 87 s hangs in the triage traces were not reproduced in any of the 42 jobs we ran afterwards. Without a reproduction there is no evidence the change helps, and some that it can hurt, so we do not keep it. If hangs return, the better fix is probably a hedged retry (start a second call after a short wait and take the first answer), which needs its own experiment.

What the card was right about: the stalls are real and the timeout was the place to look. What it did not show: that shortening the timeout is safe.

Sample sizes are 14 jobs per arm and outputs are sampled; the cost estimates and the provider's state at the time are not controlled.

## Regression fixture

None: nothing was kept. The override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` stays so the experiment can be repeated.

    assert vs["image_matches_card"].status == "pass"
    assert vs["image_no_text"].status == "violation"
'''

open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
E
